I don't want to burn figure space with GO terms.  Will present data in supplemental spreadsheets. 
The genes will be shown on rows and the columns will be go terms 
The goal will be to order the genes in some sensible fashion by clustering the go terms. 


Add diff gene column if missing 

```{r}

diff_genes <- histone_k_toc_t50 %>%
  dplyr::filter(max_cat == "P14_P56" ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(group_1 == "Dynically expressed in granule neuron lineage") %>%
  dplyr::filter(group_2 == ">2 log2FC") %>%
  dplyr::filter(t50_cat %in% c("Mid", "Late")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("_exclude", max_cat_exclude)) %>%
  dplyr::select(ensembl_gene_id)

histone_k_toc_t50 <- histone_k_toc_t50 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff_gene = case_when(
      ensembl_gene_id %in%  diff_genes$ensembl_gene_id    ~  "differentiation",
      TRUE                             ~  "other"
  )) 
```


```{r}

source("~/Dropbox/jp_seq/topGO_wrap.R")
MF_GO <- topGO_wrap(histone_k_toc_t50, "diff_gene", "mgi_symbol", topNodes = 100)

BP_GO <- topGO_wrap(histone_k_toc_t50, "diff_gene", "mgi_symbol", topNodes = 100, ontology = "BP")

MF_GO_row <- topGO_wrap(histone_k_toc_t50, "diff_gene", "mgi_symbol", topNodes = 100, genes_as_row = TRUE)

BP_GO_row <- topGO_wrap(histone_k_toc_t50, "diff_gene", "mgi_symbol", topNodes = 100, ontology = "BP", genes_as_row = TRUE)

```

Select columns to merge 
```{r}

MF_GO_ordered_annotated <- histone_k_toc_t50 %>%
  dplyr::filter(diff_gene == "differentiation") %>%
  dplyr::select(mgi_symbol, avg_fc, avg_t50, description, ensembl_gene_id, H3K27me3_single_bin) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(MF_GO_row, by = join_by(mgi_symbol == genes)) %>%
  dplyr::slice(match(MF_GO_row$genes, mgi_symbol)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(mgi_symbol))  # remove any rows where there wasn't a match in MF_GO_row

```

Need entrez id, get with biomart, tried this because getting only 370 genes when run the entrez id from bitr as below

```{r}
library(biomaRt)

# Set up the connection to the Ensembl BioMart database
ensembl <- useMart("ensembl", dataset = "mmusculus_gene_ensembl")

# Convert Ensembl to Entrez using biomaRt
entrez_mapping <- getBM(
  attributes = c("ensembl_gene_id", "entrezgene_id"),
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = diff_genes$ensembl_gene_id,
  mart = ensembl
)

# Remove any NA entries in the Entrez column
entrez_mapping <- entrez_mapping[!is.na(entrez_mapping$entrezgene_id), ]

```


```{r}
library(AnnotationHub)
ah <- AnnotationHub()
orgDb <- query(ah, c("OrgDb", "Mus musculus"))[[1]]  # Replace if needed with a more recent version

# Re-run the bitr function with the new OrgDb
gene_entrez_ah <- bitr(
  diff_genes$ensembl_gene_id, 
  fromType = "ENSEMBL", 
  toType = "ENTREZID", 
  OrgDb = orgDb
)


combined_entrez <- dplyr::left_join(gene_entrez, entrez_mapping, by = join_by("ENSEMBL" == "ensembl_gene_id"))
all_entrez_ids <- unique(c(combined_entrez$ENTREZID, entrez_mapping$entrezgene_id))

kegg_results_updated <- enrichKEGG(
  gene = all_entrez_ids,
  organism = "mmu",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

# View the summary
head(kegg_results_updated@result)
```

Get the genes associated

```{r}
# Ensure kegg_results is set to readable gene names (optional but recommended)
kegg_results_readable <- setReadable(kegg_results, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")

# Extract pathway IDs and comma-separated gene lists
pathway_gene_lists <- kegg_results_readable@result %>%
  dplyr::mutate(genes = sapply(strsplit(geneID, "/"), paste, collapse = ", ")) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, Description, genes)

# Ensure the kegg_results is set to readable gene names (optional but recommended)
kegg_results_readable <- setReadable(kegg_results, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")

# Add a column with comma-separated genes to the summary table
kegg_results_summary <- kegg_results_readable@result %>%
  dplyr::mutate(genes_list = sapply(strsplit(geneID, "/"), paste, collapse = ", "))

library(stringr)

kegg_results_final <- kegg_results_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(-geneID) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Count > 8) %>%
  dplyr::filter(FoldEnrichment > 2) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Description = str_remove(Description, fixed("- Mus musculus (house mouse)")))

```

```{r}
# Format KEGG pathway data to align with GO data structure
kegg_results_final_formatted <- kegg_results_final %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    GO.ID = ID,
    Term = Description,
    gene_number = Count,
    p_value = p.adjust,
    genes = genes_list
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    GO_ontology = "Pathway"  # Indicate that these are KEGG pathways
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(GO_ontology, GO.ID, Term, gene_number, p_value, genes)

```



Reactome

```{r}
library(ReactomePA)

reactome_results <- enrichPathway(
  gene = gene_entrez$ENTREZID,
  organism = "mouse", 
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05, 
  readable = TRUE
)




```

Setup up reactome for merging 

```{r}
# Step 1: Prepare the Reactome data to match the GO data structure
reactome_results_processed <- reactome_results@result %>%
  # Rename columns to match the GO table format
  dplyr::rename(
    GO.ID = ID,
    Term = Description,
    gene_number = Count,
    p_value = p.adjust
  ) %>%
  # Add the necessary columns for compatibility
  dplyr::mutate(
    GO_ontology = "Pathway",   # Specify ontology type as "Pathway"
    genes = str_replace_all(geneID, "/", ", "),  # Replace "/" with ", " in gene list
    Term = str_replace(Term, "- Mus musculus \\(house mouse\\)", "")  # Clean up pathway names
  ) %>%
  # Select and reorder columns to match the GO table
  dplyr::select(GO_ontology, GO.ID, Term, gene_number, p_value, genes)

reactome_results_processed <- reactome_results_processed %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_number > 8) %>%
  dplyr::filter(p_value < 0.05)


reactome_results_processed
```


We will provide 2 tables.  One that has all the GO term and pathway enrichment and a second that is a gene based table. 


Prepare final tables for export 

```{r}

BP_GO_final <- BP_GO %>% 
  dplyr::select(-pair_id, -Annotated, -Expected, -classicFisher, -topgoFisher, -set1, -gene_num) %>%
  dplyr::rename("gene_number" = Significant, "p_value" = elimFisher) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GO_ontology = "BP") %>%
  dplyr::select(GO_ontology, everything())
  
MF_GO_final <- MF_GO %>% 
  dplyr::select(-pair_id, -Annotated, -Expected, -classicFisher, -topgoFisher, -set1, -gene_num) %>%
  dplyr::rename("gene_number" = Significant, "p_value" = elimFisher) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GO_ontology = "MF") %>%
  dplyr::select(GO_ontology, everything())


All_GO_final <- rbind(BP_GO_final, MF_GO_final, kegg_results_final_formatted, reactome_results_processed)

write.table(All_GO_final, "~/Dropbox/GNP_MB_integrate/Ezh2_2022/All_GO_final.txt", sep = "\t", col.names =  TRUE)
write_xlsx(All_GO_final, "~/Dropbox/Q_research/EZH2 final/All_GO_final.xlsx")
```

Merge the gene based table 

```{r}


# Applying the function to each data frame
BP_GO_gene_based <- go_to_gene_table(BP_GO_final, "BP_term_")
KEGG_gene_based <- go_to_gene_table(kegg_results_final_formatted, "KEGG_term_")
Reactome_gene_based <- go_to_gene_table(reactome_results_processed, "Reactome_term_")


# Combine all collapsed matrices
final_combined <- BP_GO_gene_based %>%
  left_join(KEGG_gene_based, by = "genes") %>%
  left_join(Reactome_gene_based, by = "genes")

# View the final result
head(final_combined)

diff_genes_annotated_all <- MF_GO_ordered_annotated_target_TF %>%
  dplyr::left_join(final_combined, by = c("mgi_symbol" = "genes"))


write.table(diff_genes_annotated_all, "~/Dropbox/GNP_MB_integrate/Ezh2_2022/diff_genes_annotated_all.txt", sep = "\t", col.names =  TRUE)
write_xlsx(diff_genes_annotated_all, "~/Dropbox/Q_research/EZH2 final/diff_genes_annotated_all.xlsx")
```

## Text from an old verions



Many of the differentiation genes are involved in neuronal function with 181 genes impacting membrane potenial or synaptic singalling, which includes 45 ion channels and 45 transporters.  Genes involved in cell morphogenesis make up another 57 genes including cell adhesion proteins and another 28 proteins involved in the cytoskeleton. In addition to these terminal effectors of building a functional neuron we also see an increase in 50 transcription factors, which could have extensive downstream impact on transcription.
